**Tags:** `boundary`, `sandbox`

## Learning objectives

- Get comfortable with the run page, the Cluster and Logs tabs, terminals and node actions.
- Explore Boundary freely.

## Prerequisites

- None.

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boundary version | version |  | The version to run. It defaults to the newest. |
| Edition | edition | community | Only the community edition is available for now. |
| Controller count | int | 3 | How many Boundary controllers to run, from 1 to 5. They sit behind a load balancer. |

## Initial state

One network. One PostgreSQL database, db-node-1. The chosen number of controllers, node-1 and on, behind an HAProxy load balancer, lb-node-1. One worker, worker-node-1, registered through the balancer. One target host, target-node-1, running OpenSSH. The database is initialised with boundary database init, so an admin account exists with global admin grants, and a resource tree is seeded: an org scope, a project scope, a static host catalog with a host and a host set that point at the target host, and a TCP target for SSH. The Cluster tab shows the addresses, the admin login and password, the IDs of what was created, and the SSH account of the target host.

## Steps

This scenario has no steps. It is an open-ended sandbox, so it runs until you end it.
